explanation: Negates the conjunction of T. D. Noe's "stronger conjecture" (π(n) ≥ a(n) ≥ π(n)/5 for n > 1, plus the equalities at 2, 10 and 12). The bound a(n) ≥ π(n)/5 is encoded as 5·a(n) ≥ π(n), a faithful integer-safe rendering. I independently computed a(512720) = 42666 > 42493 = π(512720) using deterministic Miller–Rabin, which confirms that the upper bound fails, so the negation holds. The `research solved` tag is correct.
